interactions.comment: Would love to understand more about the stop/go gates. Were these based on customer churn, margin dilution, or something else?
interactions.reply_posted: Razn In high-velocity scaleups, stop/go gates work best when anchored strictly to contribution margin dilution and net revenue retention (NRR) rather than top-line GMV. Once customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback exceeds 12 months or legacy maintenance eats >40% of engineering bandwidth, the migration trigger must be non-negotiable.
